Smart Campus Wi-Fi Monitoring & Network Health Dashboard

Complete Architecture & Build Blueprint (local, runs in a web browser)

Audience: an AI coding agent (or a human) that will build the whole system from this document alone. Result: one project folder. npm run setup && npm start → open http://localhost:3000 in a browser. No cloud, no external accounts, no internet needed after npm install.

0. How to use this document (rules for the building agent)

  1. Follow the phases in §13 in order. Each phase has acceptance checks. Do not start a phase until the previous one passes.
  2. Do not change the stack (§2). Do not add cloud services, external APIs or paid dependencies.
  3. Tags used in this document
  4. [SPEC] – comes straight from the hackathon brief. Quoted text is verbatim from the brief.
  5. [DECISION] – the brief leaves this open; this document makes the choice. Do not re-debate it; implement it.
  6. Never invent data in the product. Real measurements come from the speed test. Demo data exists only through the seeder and is flagged is_seed = 1.
  7. Dependency rule (clean architecture, §3.2): domain imports nothing. application imports domain. infrastructure and http import application + domain. Never the reverse. Enforce with the ESLint rule in §4.3.
  8. No stubs. No TODO, no fake endpoints returning constants. If a feature is listed, it works end to end (DB → API → UI).
  9. After each phase: run npm test, npm run lint, npm run typecheck. Commit with a message naming the phase.

1. Product summary

1.1 What is being built

[SPEC] "A deployed system that allows users to run Wi-Fi speed tests, report connectivity problems, and helps IT teams monitor network health across different campus locations."

[SPEC] The end-to-end flow the system must implement:

"User Selects Location → Runs Speed Test → Network Metrics Collected → Health Score Calculated → Result Stored → Dashboard Updated → IT Team Reviews Problems"

and the final vision adds "Complaint Submitted if Needed" and "Analytics Updated".

[SPEC] "The project should not become only a normal speed-test website." → the speed test is only the data source. Complaints, outage detection, IT workflow, analytics and the intelligent features are equally required.

[DECISION] Local deployment. The brief says "deployed"; the requester wants it local in a browser. So: a single Node.js process serves the API and the built web app on one port, bound to all network interfaces so phones/laptops on the same Wi-Fi can open it (this is what makes the Wi-Fi measurement meaningful, see §5.1 note).

1.2 Flow mapped to components

1.3 Roles [SPEC]

Role code (DB) Brief's name Summary of what they can do (from the brief)
user Student / Staff User select location, run test, view result + history, submit complaints, view outage info, check health of other locations, view recent status
it_staff IT Support Staff view test results and complaints, monitor poor locations, mark issues under investigation, update status, add maintenance notes, view history, monitor outages
manager Network / IT Manager manage locations, overall health, compare buildings, speed/latency trends, recurring problems, monitor IT activity, reports & analytics
admin Administrator manage users, buildings & locations, IT staff, permissions, system-wide reports, configure health thresholds

Full permission matrix: §7.2.

2. Technology decisions [DECISION]

Chosen for: zero external services, one-command start, and being the most common stack an AI agent writes correctly.

Concern Choice Why
Runtime Node.js ≥ 20 LTS, TypeScript 5 (strict) everywhere one language front and back, shared types
Monorepo npm workspaces: apps/server, apps/web, packages/shared one npm install, shared code
HTTP framework Express 4 + helmet, cors (dev only), compression (skipped on speed-test routes), express-rate-limit, cookie-parser, pino-http familiar, minimal
Validation Zod (schemas live in packages/shared, used by server and web forms) single source of truth for payloads
Database SQLite via better-sqlite3 (file data/campus-wifi.db, WAL mode) local, zero setup, fast, synchronous = simple code
DB access Hand-written SQL in repositories, plain .sql migrations, no ORM explicit, easy to read for judges
Auth Email + password, bcryptjs hashes, JWT in an httpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie (jsonwebtoken) no external IdP
Realtime Server-Sent Events (/api/events) one-way push is all we need; no extra library
Scheduler In-process setInterval jobs (60 s) no cron daemon needed
Frontend React 18 + Vite + TypeScript, React Router 6, TanStack Query, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, react-hook-form + Zod resolver, lucide-react icons fast, charts built in
Tests Vitest (unit + integration with supertest, in-memory SQLite), Playwright (1 end-to-end flow)
Lint/format ESLint (+ eslint-plugin-boundaries), Prettier enforce the dependency rule
"AI" features Local, deterministic algorithms (robust statistics, rule-based text classification, template language generation). Optional adapter to a local LLM (Ollama) for rewording summaries; off by default works offline, explainable, reproducible in a demo

3. System architecture

3.1 Runtime view (mirrors the brief's recommended architecture)

[SPEC] "Web / Mobile Application → Backend API → Speed Test Service → Network Health Analyzer → Database → IT Support / Admin Dashboard"

3.2 Clean architecture layers (server)

Rules - domain = pure TypeScript, no fs, no Date.now() (receive time as a parameter), no DB. It lives in packages/shared/src/domain so the browser can reuse status bands and colors. - application use cases receive their dependencies via constructor (manual dependency injection in apps/server/src/container.ts). No DI framework. - Controllers contain no business logic. If it has an if about the network or complaints, it belongs in domain or a use case.

3.3 Server module map

Each module folder has the same internal shape: application/ (use cases + ports), infrastructure/ (SQLite repo), http/ (router + controller). Domain rules are in the shared package.

3.4 Local deployment view

On start, the server prints every reachable URL (localhost + each LAN IPv4) and the web app shows the LAN URL with a QR code on the Admin page (use the qrcode npm package).

5. Domain rules (pure logic in packages/shared/src/domain)

All thresholds below are defaults stored in the settings table (key health.config, outage.config) so the Administrator can change them [SPEC: "Configure network health thresholds"]. Domain functions take the config as an argument.

5.1 Speed test measurement (client engine + server probe endpoints)

[SPEC] "The speed test does not need to be as advanced as a commercial service." Measurements only need to be reasonable and consistent.

Scope note (put this text in the UI under the result): the test measures the path between this device and the campus server (Wi-Fi link + LAN). To reflect "internet" quality, run the server on a wired machine on the campus network. A phone on weak Wi-Fi will correctly score badly.

Server probe endpoints (module speedtest, authenticated, excluded from compression, always Cache-Control: no-store):

Endpoint Behavior
GET /api/speedtest/ping respond 204 immediately (no body)
GET /api/speedtest/download?bytes=N stream N bytes (1 KiB ≤ N ≤ 32 MiB) of incompressible random data from a pre-generated 1 MiB buffer reused in a loop; honour back-pressure (res.write / drain); set Content-Length; Content-Encoding: identity
POST /api/speedtest/upload read and discard the body (req.on('data'), count bytes, no body parser on this route, limit 64 MiB), reply { "received": <bytes> }

Client engine (apps/web/src/features/speedtest/engine/), run strictly in this order; quick mode (env SPEEDTEST_QUICK or ?quick=1) divides all durations by ~3:

Phase Algorithm Output
1. Ping 20 sequential GET /ping?t=<random> probes, 50 ms apart, each with a 1500 ms AbortController timeout; RTT = performance.now() delta. Drop the first sample (connection warm-up) if ≥ 5 succeeded. ping_ms = median of successful RTTs; jitter_ms = mean absolute difference of consecutive RTTs; packet_loss_pct = timeouts ÷ probes × 100 (1 decimal)
2. Download 4 parallel workers, each looping fetch('/api/speedtest/download?bytes=8388608', {cache:'no-store'}) and counting bytes from response.body.getReader(); run 8 s; ignore the first 1.5 s (TCP slow-start); stop with AbortController. download_mbps = bytes in measured window × 8 ÷ window seconds ÷ 1e6
3. Upload 3 parallel workers, each looping XMLHttpRequest POST of a 2 MiB random Uint8Array (fill via crypto.getRandomValues in 64 KiB chunks, created once); track xhr.upload.onprogress; run 6 s; ignore first 1 s. upload_mbps same formula

Live UI: progress phase label, a live speed gauge/number during download and upload, final result card. Total ≈ 20 s (≈ 8 s in quick mode).

Failure handling [SPEC: "If a speed test cannot complete, the system should show a proper message instead of storing incorrect results."]:

Condition Client behavior Server record
0 successful pings out of 20 show "Speed test could not be completed. Please check your connection and try again." (exact text from the brief) + "No internet / server unreachable" detail POST /api/tests/failures with reason=unreachable (if the server cannot be reached at all, queue the failure in memory and send on next success)
Download or upload moved 0 bytes, or a worker threw a network error before the minimum window same message, reason=download_failed / upload_failed failure row
User cancels discard silently nothing
Any failure never call POST /api/tests test_failures row only (feeds "number of recent failures", §5.2)

5.2 Health score and status [SPEC §4]

[SPEC] statuses: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor, Critical. Inputs: download, upload, ping, packet loss, number of recent failures, recent complaints.

Sub-scores (each 0–100):

log(x, cap)  = min(100, 100 * ln(1 + x) / ln(1 + cap))
linear(x,a,b)= clamp(100 * (x - a) / (b - a), 0, 100)

downloadScore = log(download_mbps, cap = 100)
uploadScore   = log(upload_mbps,   cap = 50)
pingScore     = 100 - linear(ping_ms, best = 20,  worst = 300)
lossScore     = 100 - linear(loss_pct, best = 0,  worst = 15)

baseScore     = 0.30*downloadScore + 0.15*uploadScore + 0.30*pingScore + 0.25*lossScore

penalty       = min(10, 2 * recentFailures) + min(10, 1 * recentOpenComplaints)
healthScore   = round(max(0, baseScore - penalty), 1)

recentFailures and recentOpenComplaints are counted for that location in the last 24 h (penaltyWindowHours).

Bands: ≥ 90 Excellent, 70–89.9 Good, 50–69.9 Fair, 30–49.9 Poor, < 30 Critical.

Default config JSON (settings.health.config):

{
  "caps": { "downloadMbps": 100, "uploadMbps": 50 },
  "ping": { "best": 20, "worst": 300 },
  "loss": { "best": 0, "worst": 15 },
  "weights": { "download": 0.30, "upload": 0.15, "ping": 0.30, "loss": 0.25 },
  "penalty": { "perFailure": 2, "maxFailure": 10, "perComplaint": 1, "maxComplaint": 10, "windowHours": 24 },
  "bands": { "excellent": 90, "good": 70, "fair": 50, "poor": 30 },
  "location": { "windowMinutes": 120, "maxTests": 5, "halfLifeMinutes": 30, "staleHours": 24 }
}

Validation on save: weights sum to 1 (±0.001), bands strictly descending, all numbers finite and > 0.

Reference vectors (unit-test these exactly; they reproduce the brief's own examples):

Input (down / up / ping / loss, recent complaints) baseScore healthScore Status Brief's example
36 / 14 / 28 / 1, 0 86.3 86.3 Good Computer Lab 2 → "Network Health: Good"
5.2 / 1.8 / 190 / 10, 0 35.9 35.9 Poor Library Floor 2 → "Health Score: 34 / 100, Status: Poor"
5.2 / 1.8 / 190 / 10, 2 open complaints 35.9 33.9 Poor (≈ 34, complaints lower the score)
100 / 50 / 10 / 0, 0 100 100 Excellent
0.1 / 0.1 / 300 / 15, 0 ≈ 1 ≈ 1 Critical

(Tolerance ±0.1. These numbers were computed with the formulas above.)

Location health (locationHealth.ts) – used for locations.current_status/current_score, the heatmap and "poor locations": 1. Take the location's tests from the last windowMinutes, newest first, max maxTests. 2. Weight each test w = 0.5 ^ (ageMinutes / halfLifeMinutes); base = Σ(w · baseScore) / Σw. 3. Subtract the current penalty (failures + open complaints, last 24 h). Clamp 0–100. 4. No tests in the window but some within staleHours → use the mean baseScore of the last 24 h, flag stale = true (UI shows "last tested 5 h ago"). 5. No tests within staleHours → status unknown (UI gray). unknown is the only status outside the brief's five and is used for display only.

Colors [SPEC heatmap: "Green → Good Network, Yellow → Fair Network, Red → Poor Network"]: Excellent/Good → green (Excellent darker), Fair → yellow, Poor → red, Critical → dark red, Unknown → gray. Always show the status word as well as the color (accessibility).

5.3 Outage detection [SPEC §5]

[SPEC] "If many users report the same problem in the same location, the system can create an outage warning." Example message: "Possible Wi-Fi outage detected in Library Block."

An outage is a row in outages. At most one active outage per location (partial unique index).

Open an outage when ANY rule fires (config outage.config, evaluated after every complaint, failure, test and by the scheduler):

Rule Default
R1 Complaint cluster ≥ 3 distinct users filed complaints in the same location with the same category within 30 min, category ∈ {no_internet, frequent_disconnection, website_service_unavailable, slow_internet, high_ping, weak_signal} (any category except other)
R2 Failure cluster ≥ 3 speed-test failures with reason=unreachable at the location within 15 min, from ≥ 2 distinct users
R3 Sustained critical the last 3 tests at the location are all Critical

The outage message uses the building name: "Possible Wi-Fi outage detected in {building}." (location name if the building is empty). Store cause_rule (R1/R2/R3) and counts for the UI explanation.

Resolve (automatic, scheduler + after each test): ≥ 2 consecutive tests with healthScore ≥ 50 after detected_at and no rule currently firing → set resolved_at, emit network_recovered ("Network returns to normal"). IT staff may also resolve manually (resolved_by set).

Suppression: while a maintenance window covers the location (§6, maintenance_windows), do not open new outages and do not notify "poor" transitions; tag tests taken during maintenance with during_maintenance=1.

5.4 Complaint workflow [SPEC §5]

[SPEC] "Submitted → Reviewed → Assigned → In Progress → Resolved". Categories [SPEC]: no_internet, slow_internet, high_ping, frequent_disconnection, weak_signal, website_service_unavailable, other. (Use these exact codes; display names: "No Internet", "Slow Internet", "High Ping", "Frequent Disconnection", "Weak Signal", "Website / Service Unavailable", "Other".)

Rules (complaintFlow.ts: canTransition(from, to, actorRole, isAssignee) + nextStatuses(...)): - Only forward, one step at a time. No skipping, no going back in v1. - assigned requires assigned_staff (a user with role it_staff); any of it_staff/manager/admin may assign. - in_progress and resolved may be done by the assignee, a manager or an admin (not by other IT staff). - Every transition writes a complaint_events row (+ optional note) and an activity_logs row, and notifies (§11.3). - On resolved: set resolved_at. - The reporter can attach the latest speed test (related_test_id must belong to the same user, same location, ≤ 24 h old; the UI preselects the user's latest test at that location). Complaint detail shows the attached metrics (e.g., Slow Internet, Library, Download 3.8 Mbps, Ping 170 ms, Submitted 1:35 PM).

6. Data model

Timestamps: ISO-8601 UTC strings. IDs: crypto.randomUUID(). Speeds in Mbps, ping/jitter in ms, loss in %.

6.1 ER diagram

The field names for LOCATIONS, SPEED_TESTS, COMPLAINTS and USERS are the brief's own [SPEC §7]: location_id, location_name, building, floor, description, current_status · test_id, user_id, location_id, download_speed, upload_speed, ping, packet_loss, health_score, health_status, tested_at · complaint_id, user_id, location_id, complaint_type, description, related_test_id, status, assigned_staff, created_at, resolved_at · user_id, name, email, role, account_status. Extra columns are [DECISION] additions.

6.2 Migration 001_init.sql (copy as is)

PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

CREATE TABLE users (
  user_id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name           TEXT NOT NULL,
  email          TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,
  password_hash  TEXT NOT NULL,
  role           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('user','it_staff','manager','admin')),
  account_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (account_status IN ('active','suspended')),
  created_at     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now'))
);

CREATE TABLE locations (
  location_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  location_name  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  building       TEXT NOT NULL,
  floor          INTEGER,
  description    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  current_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'
                 CHECK (current_status IN ('excellent','good','fair','poor','critical','unknown')),
  current_score  REAL,
  current_stale  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  map_x          REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 50 CHECK (map_x BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  map_y          REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 50 CHECK (map_y BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  is_active      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now'))
);

CREATE TABLE speed_tests (
  test_id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id            TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  location_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(location_id),
  download_speed     REAL NOT NULL CHECK (download_speed >= 0),
  upload_speed       REAL NOT NULL CHECK (upload_speed >= 0),
  ping               REAL NOT NULL CHECK (ping > 0),
  jitter             REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  packet_loss        REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (packet_loss BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  base_score         REAL NOT NULL,
  health_score       REAL NOT NULL CHECK (health_score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  health_status      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (health_status IN ('excellent','good','fair','poor','critical')),
  during_maintenance INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  is_seed            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  client_meta        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  tested_at          TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_tests_loc_time  ON speed_tests(location_id, tested_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_tests_user_time ON speed_tests(user_id, tested_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_tests_time      ON speed_tests(tested_at);

CREATE TABLE test_failures (
  failure_id  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  location_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(location_id),
  reason      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (reason IN ('unreachable','download_failed','upload_failed','timeout','other')),
  detail      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  occurred_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_fail_loc_time ON test_failures(location_id, occurred_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE complaints (
  complaint_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  location_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(location_id),
  complaint_type  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (complaint_type IN
    ('no_internet','slow_internet','high_ping','frequent_disconnection','weak_signal','website_service_unavailable','other')),
  description     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(description) BETWEEN 5 AND 1000),
  related_test_id TEXT REFERENCES speed_tests(test_id),
  status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'submitted'
                  CHECK (status IN ('submitted','reviewed','assigned','in_progress','resolved')),
  assigned_staff  TEXT REFERENCES users(user_id),
  ai_category     TEXT,
  ai_confidence   REAL,
  is_seed         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  resolved_at     TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX idx_compl_loc_time ON complaints(location_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_compl_status   ON complaints(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_compl_user     ON complaints(user_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE complaint_events (
  event_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  complaint_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES complaints(complaint_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  actor_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  kind         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('created','status_change','assignment','note')),
  from_status  TEXT,
  to_status    TEXT,
  note         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at   TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_cevents ON complaint_events(complaint_id, created_at);

CREATE TABLE outages (
  outage_id       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  location_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES locations(location_id),
  status          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('active','resolved')),
  cause_rule      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (cause_rule IN ('R1','R2','R3','manual')),
  message         TEXT NOT NULL,
  complaint_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  failure_count   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  detected_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
  resolved_at     TEXT,
  resolved_by     TEXT REFERENCES users(user_id)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_one_active_outage ON outages(location_id) WHERE status = 'active';

CREATE TABLE maintenance_windows (
  maintenance_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  location_id    TEXT REFERENCES locations(location_id),   -- NULL = whole campus
  title          TEXT NOT NULL,
  notes          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  starts_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  ends_at        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (ends_at > starts_at),
  created_by     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  announced      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at     TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE notifications (
  notification_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id         TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  type            TEXT NOT NULL,
  title           TEXT NOT NULL,
  body            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  entity_type     TEXT,
  entity_id       TEXT,
  is_read         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_notif_user ON notifications(user_id, is_read, created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE insights (
  insight_id  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  kind        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN
    ('problem_detected','anomaly','trend_drop','outage_risk','peak_forecast','summary','recommendation')),
  location_id TEXT REFERENCES locations(location_id),
  severity    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (severity IN ('info','warning','critical')),
  message     TEXT NOT NULL,
  data_json   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  is_active   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at  TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_active_insight ON insights(kind, COALESCE(location_id,'*')) WHERE is_active = 1;

CREATE TABLE activity_logs (
  log_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  actor_id    TEXT REFERENCES users(user_id),
  action      TEXT NOT NULL,
  entity_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  entity_id   TEXT,
  meta_json   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_activity_time ON activity_logs(created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE settings (
  key        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

insights is upserted: re-detecting the same kind for the same location updates the active row instead of inserting; when the condition clears, set is_active = 0.

Migrations: files NNN_name.sql applied in order inside a transaction, tracked in a _migrations(name, applied_at) table created by migrate.ts.

7. API contract

Base path /api. JSON in/out. Auth = httpOnly cookie cw_session. All state-changing requests must send header X-Requested-With: campus-wifi (simple CSRF defense on top of SameSite=Lax).

Error shape (every error): { "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "Human readable", "details": { "field": ["msg"] } } } Codes: VALIDATION_ERROR 400, UNAUTHENTICATED 401, FORBIDDEN 403, NOT_FOUND 404, CONFLICT 409, RATE_LIMITED 429, INTERNAL 500. Lists: ?page=1&pageSize=25 → { "items": [...], "page": 1, "pageSize": 25, "total": 130 }.

Legend for who: U user, S it_staff, M manager, A admin, * any logged-in, pub no login.

Method & path Who Purpose / notes

POST /tests validation (server is authoritative; ignores any client-supplied score): - Zod: numbers finite; 0 ≤ download,upload ≤ 10000; 0 < ping ≤ 5000; 0 ≤ jitter ≤ 5000; 0 ≤ loss ≤ 100; location_id exists and is active. - Reject with VALIDATION_ERROR if download = 0 and upload = 0 (that is a failed test, not a result). - tested_at is server time (never client time).

8. Core flows

8.1 Speed test (client ↔ server)

8.2 Ingestion pipeline (server use case SubmitSpeedTest)

All writes in one DB transaction; notifications/SSE are emitted after commit.

8.3 Complaint life cycle

9. Intelligent features (all local and deterministic)

The brief lists optional AI features: "These additional AI features are not mandatory, but they can help teams demonstrate a more intelligent and technically complete solution during judging." Implement all of them using the methods below (no model training, no internet). They run in modules/insights (orchestration + persistence) and packages/shared/src/domain (math). Config in settings.insights.config.

Schedule: onNewTest runs 9.1, 9.1b, 9.1c for that location immediately; the scheduler recomputes 9.3–9.6 every 5 minutes.

9.1 Network anomaly detection + automatic problem detection + trend detection

(a) Anomaly [SPEC "Detect unusual drops in speed, increases in latency, or abnormal network behavior."] - Baseline for a new test: same location, same local hour ±1, last 14 days, excluding the last 60 min (seeded history counts as normal history). Need ≥ 8 samples, else use all hours at that location (≥ 8), else skip. - Robust z-score: z = (x − median) / (1.4826 · MAD) (if MAD = 0 use 0.1 · median). - Anomaly if downloadZ ≤ −3 and download dropped ≥ 40 % vs median, or pingZ ≥ +3 and ping ≥ 2× median, or lossZ ≥ +3 and loss ≥ 5 %. - Insight anomaly, severity warning, message built from numbers, e.g. "Download speed at Library Floor 2 is 4.1 Mbps, 82 % below its usual 22.7 Mbps for this hour." Auto-clears (is_active=0) after 2 consecutive normal tests.

(b) Automatic Problem Detection [SPEC "If a location repeatedly shows poor results, the system should flag it."] — if ≥ 3 of the last 5 tests (last 24 h) at a location are poor or critical → insight problem_detected, severity warning (critical if ≥ 4), message exactly: "Possible network problem detected in {location_name}." Clears when the location's status is Fair or better.

(c) Performance Trend Detection [SPEC] — mean healthScore of the last 3 tests < 0.75 × mean of the previous 14 days at that location (≥ 8 samples) → insight trend_drop, message exactly: "Network performance is lower than the usual average for this location." (append the numbers in data_json; show them as a tooltip).

9.2 Complaint classification [SPEC "Automatically classify user complaints into categories"]

classifier.ts: lower-case, strip punctuation, match weighted keyword/phrase lists per category; score = Σ weights; confidence = top / (top + second + 0.5) (0–1); returns the top category and alternatives. Seed lists (extend freely, keep in one const KEYWORDS):

Category Phrases (weight)
no_internet "no internet" 3, "not connected" 2, "can't connect" 2, "cannot connect" 2, "offline" 2, "no connection" 3, "internet is down" 3, "down" 1
slow_internet "slow" 3, "loading" 1, "buffering" 2, "takes forever" 2, "very slow" 3, "speed" 1, "lag" 1, "crawling" 2
high_ping "ping" 3, "latency" 3, "lag" 2, "delay" 2, "laggy" 2, "video call" 1, "gaming" 1, "high ms" 2
frequent_disconnection "disconnect" 3, "keeps dropping" 3, "drops" 2, "every few minutes" 3, "keeps disconnecting" 3, "logging out" 1, "reconnect" 2, "unstable" 2
weak_signal "weak signal" 3, "low signal" 3, "signal" 2, "one bar" 2, "poor coverage" 3, "no signal" 2, "dead zone" 3, "range" 1
website_service_unavailable "website" 2, "can't open" 2, "not loading" 2, "portal" 2, "lms" 2, "email not" 2, "site down" 3, "dns" 2, "blocked" 1, "service unavailable" 3
other fallback when top score < 2

Behavior: the user's chosen complaint_type is authoritative. The classifier result is stored in ai_category/ai_confidence and (a) pre-selects the category in the form as the user types (debounced POST /complaints/classify), (b) shows IT a "AI suggests: High Ping (82 %)" chip when it differs from the user's choice, (c) is used instead of other for outage rule R1 when the user chose other and confidence ≥ 0.6. Example check: "Wi-Fi disconnects every few minutes in Lab 3" → frequent_disconnection.

9.3 Outage prediction [SPEC "Identify patterns that may indicate a location is likely to experience a network problem."]

Risk score per location, 0–100, recomputed every 5 min:

risk = 40 * clamp01(-slope / 10)                 # slope = linear-regression slope of healthScore per test over the last 10 tests (points per test)
     + 25 * failureRate                           # failures / (failures + tests) in last 3 h
     + 20 * clamp01(complaints3h / 5)             # complaints in last 3 h
     + 15 * clamp01(anomalies6h / 3)              # active/recent anomaly insights

risk ≥ 70 high, 40–69 medium, else low. Insight outage_risk (warning for medium, critical for high) with message like "Library Floor 2 shows a falling trend with 4 complaints in 3 hours. Outage risk: high (78)." Require ≥ 4 tests or ≥ 2 complaints in the window, otherwise no prediction.

9.4 Peak usage prediction [SPEC "Predict times when Wi-Fi performance is likely to decrease because of high usage."]

  • Build a hour-of-week profile (7 × 24) from the last 28 days: median healthScore, mean download, and test count per cell (campus-wide and per location).
  • "Usage" proxy = test count; "expected performance" = median score. A cell is a predicted dip when its median score ≤ the location's 25th-percentile score and it has ≥ 5 samples.
  • GET /insights/predictions returns the next 24 h as 24 rows {hour, expectedScore, expectedDownload, isDip} per requested location (default: campus-wide), plus the top 3 dip windows merged into ranges (e.g. "12:00–14:00").
  • Smooth with a 3-hour moving average before ranking.

9.5 AI network summary [SPEC example: "Library Floor 2 experienced high latency and poor download speed between 12 PM and 2 PM for the last three days."]

  1. For each location, for the last 7 days, find contiguous hours where the median score < 50 (Poor/Critical) with ≥ 3 samples.
  2. If the same hour-range recurs on ≥ 3 consecutive days → emit a sentence. Choose adjectives from the data: ping median > 100 ms → "high latency"; download median < 10 Mbps → "poor download speed"; loss median > 3 % → "packet loss"; join with "and".
  3. Sentence template: "{location} experienced {issues} between {startHour} and {endHour} for the last {n} days." (12-hour clock with AM/PM).
  4. Add campus-level sentences: number of poor locations now, worst location, active outages, complaint spikes versus the 7-day average.
  5. Optional LLM rewording: if LLM_PROVIDER=ollama and a model is set, call LlmProvider.rewrite(text) with a 3 s timeout; on any error return the template text. Never let the LLM add facts: the prompt says "rewrite without changing any numbers, names or times".

9.6 Problem location detection + improvement recommendation [SPEC "Suggest which locations should be inspected first based on performance history and complaint volume."]

priority = 0.45 * (100 - currentScore)                       # current badness (stale → use 24 h mean)
         + 0.25 * poorShare7d * 100                          # share of poor/critical tests in 7 days
         + 0.20 * normalize(complaints7d, 0..max over locations) * 100
         + 0.10 * (activeOutage ? 100 : recurringDays14d >= 3 ? 70 : 0)

Return the ranked list with a reason string built from the largest contributing factors, e.g. "1. Library Floor 2 – priority 82: score 34 (Poor), 12 complaints in 7 days, outage active." This also powers "Most problematic locations" in analytics and "Problem Location Detection" (combines test results and complaints).

10.3 Frontend rules

  • api/client.ts: one fetch wrapper adding credentials:'include', X-Requested-With, JSON handling and error normalization; on 401 → redirect to /login.
  • One TanStack Query hook per endpoint; SSE events invalidate the relevant query keys (dashboard.updated → ['dashboard'], ['locations']; complaint.updated → ['complaints'], etc.).
  • Forms: react-hook-form + the same Zod schemas imported from packages/shared.
  • Every list has loading, empty and error states. Every chart has an accessible text alternative (a table toggle).
  • Responsive: usable at 360 px width (the speed test is run from phones).
  • Design tokens (Tailwind theme): status colors excellent #15803d, good #22c55e, fair #eab308, poor #ef4444, critical #991b1b, unknown #9ca3af; neutral UI otherwise.
  • Format helpers: speeds 36 Mbps (≤ 10 → 1 decimal), ping 28 ms, loss 1%, dates in CAMPUS_TZ.

11. Notifications, security, error handling

11.1 Security checklist [SPEC §9: authentication, role-based access, input validation, secure admin access]

  • Passwords: bcryptjs cost 10, min length 8. Never log passwords/tokens.
  • Cookie: httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, secure only when NODE_ENV=production and HTTPS (local HTTP must work). JWT expiry 8 h.
  • helmet defaults; CORS disabled in production (same origin), enabled for http://localhost:5173 in dev.
  • All SQL via prepared statements with bound parameters. No string-built SQL, except whitelisted column names for sorting.
  • Zod validation on every body/query/param; unknown keys stripped.
  • Rate limits: login 10/min/IP; POST /tests 1 per 15 s per user; POST /complaints 10/hour per user; probe endpoints 120/min per user.
  • RBAC middleware on every route (default deny: a route without requirePermission or requireAuth fails a startup assertion).
  • Admin safety: last admin cannot be demoted/suspended; admin cannot change own role; every admin/staff action logged to activity_logs.
  • Output: text rendered by React (escaped). Never dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

11.2 Error handling [SPEC §9]

  • Central Express error handler → shape in §7. Unknown errors → 500 INTERNAL with a request id, details only in logs.
  • Speed-test failure messages: §5.1. Unavailable internet/server during other calls: the web api/client shows a banner "Cannot reach the server. Check your Wi-Fi connection." and retries with TanStack Query defaults.

11.3 Notification rules [SPEC §9 list]

Event (type) Trigger Recipients Text (title)
complaint_submitted complaint created all it_staff + manager "New complaint: {category} at {location}"
complaint_assigned transition → assigned assignee, reporter "Complaint assigned to {staff}"
complaint_resolved transition → resolved reporter "Your complaint at {location} was resolved"
location_degraded location status enters poor/critical (and not in maintenance) it_staff, manager "{location} is now {status}"
outage_detected outage opened it_staff, manager, admin; plus users who tested/complained at that location in the last 24 h "Possible Wi-Fi outage detected in {building}."
maintenance_scheduled maintenance created all active users "Maintenance scheduled: {title}"
network_recovered outage resolved or location back to Fair+ same as degraded/outage recipients "Network returns to normal at {location}"

Dedupe: do not send the same (type, entity_id, recipient) more than once in 10 minutes.

11.4 Realtime (SSE)

GET /api/events keeps the connection open (text/event-stream, heartbeat comment every 25 s). SseHub stores connections by userId and role. Events (JSON data):

Event name Sent to Payload
notification the recipient the notification row
dashboard.updated all connected { location_id }
complaint.updated staff + reporter { complaint_id, status }
outage.opened / outage.resolved all { outage_id, location_id, message }
insight.updated staff+ { kind, location_id }

The browser EventSource reconnects automatically; on reconnect the web app invalidates all queries.

11.5 Scheduler jobs (infrastructure/scheduler)

Job Interval Does
refreshLocationStatuses 60 s recompute current_status/score/stale for every active location (so "stale" and "unknown" appear without new tests)
evaluateOutages 60 s rules R1–R3 + auto-recovery for every location
announceMaintenance 60 s send maintenance_scheduled for windows created but not yet announced; when a window ends, trigger a fresh status refresh
refreshInsights 5 min §9.3–9.6 recompute; deactivate cleared insights
purge daily delete read notifications > 30 days
All jobs are idempotent and wrapped in try/catch (an error in one job must not stop the others).

12.2 Locations [SPEC §6 examples] and synthetic profiles

Create exactly these locations (building · floor):

Location Building Floor Base down / up (Mbps) Base ping (ms) Base loss (%) Pattern
Computer Lab 1 Computer Labs 1 42 / 18 24 0.3 stable, good
Computer Lab 2 Computer Labs 1 36 / 14 28 1 stable, good
Computer Lab 3 Computer Labs 2 28 / 10 45 2 disconnection complaints, mid quality
Library Floor 1 Library Block 1 24 / 9 60 2 dips 12–14
Library Floor 2 Library Block 2 6 / 2 160 8 poor 12:00–14:00 for the last 3+ days, many complaints

Administration Block Administration 1 45 / 20 20 0.2 excellent

map_x/map_y laid out on a 0–100 canvas so the heatmap looks like a campus (labs top-left, library center, hostel bottom-right, etc.).

12.3 Generated history

  • 14 days back, 40–250 tests/day weighted toward 08:00–18:00 and the evening for the hostel; across the 12 student users; metrics = base × time-of-day factor × random noise (±15 %, log-normal), scores computed with the real health.ts (never hard-coded); is_seed=1.
  • Complaints: ≈ 60 over 14 days, heavier at Library Floor 2 and Hostel Block, realistic descriptions (e.g. "Wi-Fi disconnects every few minutes in Lab 3"), mixed statuses (about a third resolved, with events and assignees), plus ≈ 18 currently open so the dashboard resembles the brief ("Open Complaints: 18", "Poor Locations: 4").
  • A few failures and one resolved past outage; one future maintenance window.
  • After generation call the same services the app uses (refreshLocationStatuses, refreshInsights) so statuses and insights are populated.
  • Seeder is idempotent (INSERT OR IGNORE on stable ids / refuses if users exist unless --force).

12.4 Demo scripts

  • npm run simulate – logs in as a student (service layer, not HTTP), posts a random realistic test for a random location every 3 s (honors profiles above) → the dashboard moves live.
  • npm run simulate:outage -- --location "Library Floor 2" – files 4 no_internet complaints from 4 different students and 3 unreachable failures within a minute → rule R1/R2 opens an outage, notifications and SSE fire. Re-run npm run simulate:recover -- --location "Library Floor 2" to post 3 good tests → "Network returns to normal".

14. Testing strategy

Level Tooling What
Unit (domain) Vitest every function in domain/ with table-driven cases; property checks: scores always in 0–100, monotonic (better metrics never lower the score), classifier deterministic
Integration (API) Vitest + supertest + :memory: SQLite via createApp(container) every endpoint: happy path, validation error, 401, 403, 404; pipeline side-effects (rows, notifications)
Engine Vitest + fake timers + mocked fetch/XMLHttpRequest ping stats, loss calculation, warm-up exclusion, failure mapping
End to end Playwright against npm start with SPEEDTEST_QUICK=true and a fresh seeded DB one scenario: student runs test and files complaint; IT reviews → assigns → resolves; manager sees analytics
Non-functional scripts 100 concurrent POST /tests do not corrupt data; dashboard summary responds < 300 ms on the seeded data

Test clock: every use case and domain function takes now: Date (or a Clock port). Never call new Date() inside domain code.

17. Assumptions, gaps and things the brief does not say

Stated openly so the building agent does not guess differently:

  1. Web vs mobile: the brief says "Web or Mobile Application". This blueprint chooses web (responsive, usable from phones in a browser), as the requester asked for a local web-browser system.
  2. Local vs deployed: the brief says "A deployed system". This blueprint is local-first (LAN-reachable). Hosting publicly is out of scope; the same build can run on any machine with Node 20.
  3. What the speed test measures: device ↔ this server. The brief does not say whether to measure against the public internet. Measuring against the local server isolates Wi-Fi/LAN quality, which suits "campus Wi-Fi monitoring". I do not know what the organizers expect for internet-facing tests; if they want that, only the base URL of the three probe endpoints in engine/ changes.
  4. Browser limits: browsers cannot send ICMP, so "ping" is an HTTP round trip and packet loss is the share of timed-out HTTP probes. This is "reasonable" per the brief but is not identical to OS ping.
  5. Numeric thresholds (score weights, band cutoffs, outage rule counts, AI limits) are [DECISION] defaults. The brief only gives example inputs/outputs (reproduced in §5.2 reference vectors). They are all admin-configurable.
  6. Brief's sample numbers (e.g. "Tests Today: 245") are illustrations; the seeder only tries to produce a similar-looking dashboard, it does not hard-code those numbers.
  7. Location names: the brief mentions "Library", "Library Floor 2", "Library Block" and "Lab 3" inconsistently. This blueprint models them as building Library Block with locations Library Floor 1/2 and Computer Lab 3.
  8. Mobile app/APK: not built.
  9. Not specified in the brief (so deliberately minimal): email/SMS delivery of notifications (in-app + SSE only), password reset by email (an admin resets a password with PATCH /admin/users/:id { new_password }), multi-campus tenancy, file uploads, internationalization.
  10. Optional LLM: I did not verify any specific local model; the Ollama adapter is optional and the system is fully functional without it.
